content_description: Name, represent and order numbers to at least 20 using physical and virtual materials.
Recognise, represent and order numbers to at least 1000 using physical and digital tools.
Recognise, represent and partition natural numbers using standard and non-standard groupings.
Recognise and extend the application of place value to tenths and hundredths.
Interpret, compare and order numbers with more than two decimal places.
Recognise situations that can be modelled by integers and represent them on a number line.
Represent natural numbers as products of prime factors; use index notation.
Recognise and use variables; create algebraic expressions from worded descriptions.
Recognise irrational numbers and terminating/recurring decimals; locate on the number line.
Create and use algebraic expressions and formulas; apply the distributive law.
Solve problems involving the area and perimeter of composite shapes.
Apply the exponent laws to numerical expressions with integer exponents.
Apply algebraic properties to rearrange, expand and factorise linear and simple quadratic expressions.
Solve linear equations and inequalities; solve simple quadratic equations.
Understand that texts can take many forms and communicate meaning.
Discuss characters and events in texts and share personal responses.
Navigate and read texts using comprehension strategies to build literal and inferred meaning.
Identify and explain how authors use language features to represent ideas and characters.
Understand how coherence is created through the organisation of ideas and cohesive devices.
Understand how coherence is created in complex texts through cohesive devices and text structure.
Analyse and evaluate how language features and structures position readers.
Observe the properties and behaviour of familiar objects and living things.
Investigate how forces can change the motion and shape of objects.
Investigate the transfer and transformation of energy in simple systems.
Classify and organise diverse organisms based on observable features.
Analyse the properties of matter using the particle model.
Explain the role of body systems in maintaining stable internal conditions.
Examine the significance of colonial events and the experiences of different groups.
Investigate how ancient societies were organised and governed.
Investigate strategies that promote wellbeing, safety and respectful relationships.
Design and produce a solution that meets identified needs and criteria for success.
Devise and shape drama using the elements to communicate meaning to an audience.
Recognise, represent and order numbers to at least 120.
Compare and order the duration of events and sequence days of the week.
Recognise and explain the connection between addition and subtraction as inverse operations.
Choose appropriate metric units for length, mass and capacity and convert between them.
Interpret and compare data displays including side-by-side column graphs.
Solve problems involving the surface area and volume of right prisms and cylinders.
Apply deductive reasoning to proofs involving triangles and angles.
Read decodable and predictable texts using phonic and word-recognition knowledge.
Discuss how authors use language to create imagery and character.
Analyse how evaluative language positions readers and shapes argument.
Observe changes to living things, objects and the daily and seasonal environment.
Investigate the observable properties of solids, liquids and gases.
Explain the role of DNA and genes in cell division and inheritance.
Describe how communities remember and celebrate significant events.
Investigate landforms and landscapes and the processes that shape them.
Explain how markets allocate resources and influence decision-making.
Design and implement simple algorithms involving branching and iteration.
Design and validate solutions using a general-purpose programming language.
Describe strategies to keep safe and seek help in a range of situations.
Refine and apply movement skills and tactics in a range of physical activities.
Develop and perform music using rhythm, pitch and dynamics to express ideas.
Develop and refine artworks using visual conventions, materials and techniques.
Exchange information about self, family and interests in the target language.
Use comprehension strategies to build meaning from a range of texts.
